You are reviewing ONE SLICE of a build in the repository at /home/user/adss-2026-09-07.
The slice is the range claude/adss-slice-03-shipped-orders-and-days-to-ship..claude/adss-slice-04-revenue-per-order-month. Use `git diff claude/adss-slice-03-shipped-orders-and-days-to-ship..claude/adss-slice-04-revenue-per-order-month` and
`git log claude/adss-slice-03-shipped-orders-and-days-to-ship..claude/adss-slice-04-revenue-per-order-month` to see exactly what changed. Read whatever else you need.

The system is an "Analytical Data Storage System" with three layers, one direction of flow:
  DAS (das/, schemas das__raw + das__staged) -> DAB (dab/, schemas dab, dab__stage, dab__meta)
  -> DAR (dar/, schema dar__uss) -> destinations/ (a marimo page).
Flow rules, absolute: analytical usage reads ONLY dar__uss; dar reads only dab; dab reads only das.

Slice 4 adds a third entity (ORDER_LINE) at a FINER GRAIN than the order, a derived measure
(REVENUE), an inherited event date, a composed composite key, and the fan-out proof.

Ground rules for your review:
- Be specific. A finding names a file and a line and says what breaks and when.
- Do not report style preferences, or things the repository's own tools already enforce
  (ruff, ty, sqlfluff, yamllint, pytest all pass on this head -- verify that if you like).
- Do not report anything that is already written down as a known limitation in
  docs/adr/, docs/deviations.md, or the question documents. Read them before reporting.
- Prefer ONE real finding to five speculative ones. An empty report is a valid report.


YOUR LENS: ORDINARY CORRECTNESS. Review the diff as a careful engineer reviewing a pull
request. Bugs, edge cases, wrong logic, things that work on this data and not on the next.

Particular things worth attacking in this slice:
- src/adss/uss.py: the inherited-date CTE and the stage CTE. What happens with two edges to
  the same entity, an event dated by an entity two hops away, a parent with no history row,
  a pair whose eff_tmstp is after the child's observation time?
- src/adss/question.py: the new parse-tree aggregate refusal. What legitimate query does it
  wrongly refuse? What illegitimate one does it accept? What happens with a CTE, a set
  operation, a lateral join, a macro?
- src/adss/checks.py: measure_checks and composed_key_checks. What contract or mapping shape
  makes them emit SQL that does not run, or a check that cannot fail?
- src/adss/das.py: the ROW() change to the composite key check.
- The interaction between the two writers into checks/ and their sweeps: can one command
  still delete a file the other generates?

Report real defects with the file, the line, and the input that triggers them.

content.content:
ca3f329 docs(skills): write down what the second grain taught
The DAR skill's central rule said keys inherit and measures do not, and left it there. It now
carries the measurement -- 2,155 line rows against an order's freight that does not move -- and
the half that is false beside it: the bridge protects the measure column and not the attribute
it was made from, so one join and one sum over the peripheral returns 207,306.10 against a true
64,942.69. A third query-time rule follows, because the first two did not cover it.

Also the inherited date, which is the other thing this slice added and the one whose failure is
invisible: a row whose inherited date does not resolve gets no bridge row, filtered where the
date was resolved rather than where the event's own date is, because the alternative arrives
dated null and is dropped by the calendar's inner join -- which looks exactly like the rule
working.

The destination skill gains two rules learned by getting them wrong. A page invents no fact: no
currency symbol where the model records no currency. And a series has to stop somewhere, so the
period it stops inside is short rather than small -- fade it, caption it, and derive which one
it is from the answer rather than from a date the page was told.

The ADSS skill gains the one that has now cost twice: run the mutation before the ADR's
Confirmation claims one. A confirmation naming a test that could not fail for the reason given
is worse than no confirmation, because it stops anybody looking again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019rspwWhmXfxoTvKg5jmNWh

---
9378ffe feat(destination): present the revenue, and mark the month the recording stops inside
Bars rather than a line: the question is how much was taken in each month, not the shape of a
path between them. One series, so no legend -- the heading above names it.

The last bar is the one worth the code. The recording ends on 1998-05-06, so that month is six
days long: 14 orders against 74 in April. Drawn at full strength beside twenty-two whole months
it reads as a collapse in demand, and a reader would act on it. It is faded, captioned beneath,
and flagged in the tooltip, so the distinction is never carried by the fade alone -- and the
page derives it from the answer rather than from a date it was told, because a destination that
invents a fact is the one thing this layer must not do.

That artefact is not new to this slice. Every question here spans the same 23 months and the
same short last one; it is loud in a bar chart of a single magnitude in a way it is not in a
heatmap, which is the picture doing its job.

No currency symbol anywhere, and the page says why: nothing in the source records which
currency this is, so a symbol would be an invented fact on the artefact the slice is accepted
on. The headline names the best WHOLE month for the same reason -- the partial one cannot win a
comparison it was not in.

Rendered twice, byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019rspwWhmXfxoTvKg5jmNWh

---
c25a81f feat(questions): ask what the business took, and answer it at the line's grain
The fourth question, and the first whose answer is computed at a grain finer than the order.
Both queries agree row for row over 23 months: 2,155 lines, 1,265,793.0395.

What the slice is actually for is written into the question rather than left in a record
nobody reading the answer would open. Freight is 64,942.69 over the whole bridge and per month
alike, though 2,155 line rows now carry an order key -- which is the property D-0001 has been
carried on since slice one, measured for the first time. Beside it, the query that breaks the
other half: one join and one sum over the order peripheral's own freight column returns
207,306.10, and it was already wrong at 128,897.71 before this slice existed.

The register is corrected in two places. Its review section said the finer grain arrives in
slice 4 and that this is where the argument stops being carried on assertion; it has arrived,
and what it found was that the argument was half wrong -- which three slices of re-reading the
entry had not. That is the clause about assertion earning its place rather than being wisdom
nobody acted on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019rspwWhmXfxoTvKg5jmNWh

---
68cf258 feat(dab): count a composed key against the parts it was composed from
ADR 0010's other half, and the half that matters. A separator argument is a prediction about
what the parts can hold; this is a measurement over what actually landed, so a separator that
is wrong for this data says so on the build that loaded it.

The parts are counted as a tuple and the composition as the single value the engine keys on.
Two source rows that compose to one key make the second count smaller, and the entity that
disappears takes its measures with it -- silently, because every presentation view above it
shows one row where there should be two.

Generated only where the source key is composite. Where it is one column the mapping simply
names it, and counting a thing against itself is a check that cannot fail.

It is run against the shape ADR 0010 names as the one that would break it: a separator-less
concatenation over parts whose lengths vary, where (1, 23) and (12, 3) become one line. A
fourth test pins the reason this is a measurement rather than an argument -- the same
separator-less composition over parts that happen not to collide passes, because the check
reports what landed and not what somebody predicted would land. Three mutations of the
generator were run and all three fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019rspwWhmXfxoTvKg5jmNWh

---
5a56849 feat(questions): refuse an answer query that aggregates what the bridge does not protect
The other half of ADR 0012. A numeric attribute that is also a measure's source is published
twice -- once as a measure the bridge protects with a typed null on every branch that does not
own it, and once as a plain column of a peripheral, protected by nothing. One join and one sum
over the second returns 207,306.10 where the truth is 64,942.69, and it looks like an answer.

So an answer query aggregates measure columns and nothing else, and this repository's questions
are run through that rule.

It reads the engine's parse tree rather than the SQL text. A cast around the sum is what every
answer query here already writes, a window multiplies exactly as a group does, and the set of
aggregate function names is the engine's rather than one kept by hand -- three ways a text rule
would have passed a wrong number, and the third is the one nobody would have noticed. An
unparseable answer query is refused here too, rather than at the next build after a page has
been written against it.

Two deliberate strictnesses. count(*) over the bridge counts measurement events rather than the
thing asked about, and doubles the moment an entity has two events. An aggregate over a DISTINCT
peripheral column cannot be multiplied by a fan-out and is refused anyway, because narrowing the
rule to the aggregates that can actually be wrong is a rule nobody can apply without already
knowing which those are.

Four mutations of the refusal were run: doing nothing, ignoring windows, allowing an empty
aggregate, and looking at only the first of an aggregate's columns. All four fail the suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019rspwWhmXfxoTvKg5jmNWh

---
b63d9cb feat(dar): check on every build that a measure sits only on its own event's rows
test_fan_out.py proves the property with numbers on a warehouse the test builds. This carries
the same property, as a mechanism, onto the warehouse that was actually built -- which is where
a wrong number would be believed rather than caught.

One generated check per measure, and by EVENT rather than by stage. Two events on one entity
share a stage, so a per-stage check would let an order's shipment measure sit on its placement
row and report nothing at all -- and that is the likelier of the two defects, because every
branch of the union comes off the same stage's CTE and the fan-out shape needs a second grain
before it can exist. There is a test for exactly that case, and it is the one a weaker check
would pass.

It counts leaks only. A measure that is null everywhere would pass here and is not this check's
to catch: a bridge that lost its rows disagrees with the source, which is what the question
checks already compare on every build.

Both writers into checks/ now know these files, so a DAS command does not delete what a DAR
command wrote. The cost is that a DAS command reads the declarations to learn what it must not
touch, which is the same cost the relationship checks already imposed with the model.

Forty checks pass on the real build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

b3cde73 feat(dab): model the order line, at the grain the order is not
A line is one kind of goods on one order, and it is the first entity here at a finer grain
than the one above it. That is what makes slice four the first slice able to test the property
the whole shared star schema rests on rather than assert it.

Nothing on an order form identifies a line, so its key is composed from the order and the
product and then measured rather than argued about: 2155 lines, 2155 distinct keys, no
separator collision (ADR 0010). The check that says so is generated from the contract, so a
source that later reuses a separator inside an id fails the build instead of quietly merging
two lines.

REVENUE is modelled where the two vocabularies are already bound rather than in the business
model, which has no expression language, or in the star schema, which is generated (ADR 0007).
It is quantity times the agreed price less the discount, and it is named for the entity that
owns it and the unit it is in (ADR 0008).

The line has no day of its own. It inherits the order's, along the same edge and at the same
instant as the key, which is ADR 0009's whole point: a line asked for on the day the order was
accepted, not on a day nobody recorded.

e54b0ec fix(das): count a composite key as one value, and prove it by running the check
Slice one already fixed this: count(DISTINCT a, b) is not a function DuckDB has, so a
contract with two key columns emitted a check that cannot run -- and an unrunnable check
aborts the whole run before a single finding is printed. The fix was grouping parentheses,
and the formatter removed them again as redundant on the next regeneration. It has been
broken since, invisibly, because no contract had a composite key until this slice.

The parts are made into one value with ROW(), which is a function call the formatter has no
licence to unwrap.

What makes this stay fixed is not the change but the test. The old one read the emitted
string, so it agreed with a generator whose output the formatter then broke. This one formats
the check the way the build formats it, creates a table with two key columns, and executes
it: two distinct tuples are not a duplicate and a repeated tuple is. Any later step that
unwraps the value again fails here instead of at the next regeneration.

9c80d3d test(dar): prove a parent's measure is not multiplied by its children
The property D-0001 has been carried on since slice one, argued in ADR 0002 and unprovable
until now: keys inherit along a many-to-one edge and measures do not. Three slices had one
grain each, so no measure *could* multiply however the join was written, and both records
said so rather than claiming a check nobody had written.

Two grains exist now. Two parents worth 100.50 and 50.25, three children between them: the
bridge returns 150.75 and not 251.25, both grains are right in one scan, the coarser measure
is null on every finer row while the inherited key is not, and the parent total does not
move when a parent gains five children. It runs the generated SQL against a warehouse it
builds rather than reading the SQL for substrings, because a substring assertion would pass
a generator that emitted the right typed nulls in the wrong branch.

That it can fail is measured. The generator was mutated to make a measure inherit exactly as
a key does -- carried along the edge, selected by the stage, treated as the branch's own --
which emits SQL DuckDB accepts and returns 402.00 where the truth is 150.75. All four
assertions fail together. That mutation was run because two ADR confirmations in the last
slice named tests that could not have failed for the reason given, and the fix for that is
to run the mutation rather than to describe one.

A fifth test asserts the half of D-0001's argument that is false: summing the peripheral's
attribute over the same join returns 251.25. It is asserted rather than lamented, because a
reader who trusts the register needs to meet it here and not in a report.

c8034f2 feat(dar): let a stage inherit its date, and record the lines that need one
The generator half of ADR 0009. date_attribute may now name <ENTITY>.<ATTRIBUTE>, and the date
is resolved in the same CTE and at the same instant as the key -- off the same parent row the
walk had already found. An unqualified name still means the event's own entity, which is every
event declared so far.

What the record promised and the first draft did not do: a row whose inherited date does not
resolve gets no bridge row. The version CTE filters its own date, and an inherited one is not
there to filter, so the stage filters where it was resolved. Without it the row would reach the
bridge dated null and the calendar's inner join would drop it -- which looks exactly like the
rule working, and is not.

Four mutations are caught, and two of them only after the tests were sharpened. Asserting that
the date appears in the right CTE said nothing about where the STAGE reads it from, so taking
it from the event's own entity stayed green; and asserting the parent's column said nothing
about the as-of predicate, so an unbounded join to the parent's history stayed green too. Both
now fail. A date on an entity no edge reaches is refused by name, with the edges that do exist
listed, rather than by the bare KeyError that used to come out of the model.

Also records the order lines: 2155 of them, 2155 distinct composite keys, and a discount
recorded as a decimal rather than a double per ADR 0011 -- so a NaN fails at the cast instead
of becoming a month's revenue that both answers agree on.

c20a748 docs(adr): prove the property D-0001 rests on, and name the half of it that is false
Slice 4 is the first with two grains, so it is the first that can test what D-0001 has been
carried on since slice 1: that the fan trap cannot occur in one shared star schema. It half
holds, and the half that does not was already live before this slice.

The measures are safe, structurally, and this is the first demonstration of it. Over 830 order
rows and 2155 line rows, freight is 64,942.69 and revenue 1,265,793.0395 -- whole bridge, no
filter, and per order month alike. 2155 line rows carry an order key and freight does not move.

The peripherals are not safe, and the query that breaks them is one join -- the same join two
shipped questions already write. sum(order.freight_charge) over the bridge returns 207,306.10
against a true 64,942.69, because freight_charge is a published column of the order peripheral.
So any NUMBER attribute that is also a measure's source is in dar__uss twice: once protected by
a typed null on every branch that does not own it, once protected by nothing. Freight, ship lag
and revenue are all in that position.

And it was live at slice 3 already, undetected: on the warehouse shipped in PR #3, before any
line existed, the same query returns 128,897.71, because ORDER had two events. Slice 4 does not
introduce the trap; it raises it from 1.98x to 3.19x and makes it reachable from another
entity's stage, which is what a fan trap actually is.

Removing the column was rejected -- a number on a peripheral is how a reader filters or sorts,
and breaking the good use to prevent the bad one makes the peripheral a worse description than
the entity has. A query-time rule alone was rejected too: ADR 0002 already publishes two and a
third would be true, unread and unenforced.

What can be enforced is narrower and worth having. Every number this system publishes goes
through a question's answer query, and those are files this repository owns and already checks.
So an answer query may not aggregate a peripheral's column; it aggregates the measure columns,
which are the ones the bridge protects. A person at a SQL prompt can still do as they like, and
the register now says that rather than implying otherwise.

D-0001 does not close. Its exit condition is a second consumer needing isolation, and a fourth
question read by one more persona is not that. Closing it now would be closing it for a reason
that is not its own exit condition, which is how a register becomes decoration. What changes is
its Why, which has said "cannot occur" since slice 1 and now says which half.

3efd05b docs(adr): record a source float as a decimal, and say why exactness is not the reason
Discount is Edm.Single, the first float this system has met, and it feeds revenue. The contract
vocabulary has DOUBLE and DECIMAL and no REAL, so neither option transcribes what the source
declares -- both are a choice, and section 1.1's usual instruction does not settle it.

Two builds, one with each type, are indistinguishable on this data: every DAR value identical,
zero of 2155 revenue rows differing, both acceptance queries agreeing either way. So arguing
from exactness would be arguing from a magnitude this source cannot produce.

What does distinguish them is where a bad value fails. A NaN through a DOUBLE contract becomes a
NaN revenue, and a NaN anywhere in a sum makes the whole month NaN -- in both answers alike,
because both derive from the same landed value. The check agrees, the gate is green, and a
month's revenue is not a number. A DECIMAL contract refuses the record at the cast, which is
where a contract is supposed to refuse things.

It also stops the answer side resting on a coercion nobody wrote. The float currently stops at
the engine's own DECIMAL(28,8) column, silently, and nothing in this repository names that --
so every question's exactness has been a vendor's choice rather than ours.

Two things measured while deciding. ADR 0007 predicted that summing floats is order-dependent;
this slice supplies the witness on its own measure -- the same 2155 revenue values in three
orders give three answers. And slice 3's exactness check is silent on all of it, because both
sides launder the float before it is seen: the answer side is widened by the engine, and every
control query already casts. It defends against a float in an answer, not a float in a source.

Registered as D-0002, because the contract now says something the source's metadata does not.

681d37b docs(adr): decide the composite key by measuring it, not by arguing about separators
M2 has permitted a concat of casts with a separator since slice 1, and warned about the
collision one without a separator causes. Nothing had a composite key until now, so the clause
has been review-only for three slices. A probe built this slice four times over and measured
what the rule was asserting.

The collision cannot happen in this data at all: every OrderId is five digits, so the split
point is never ambiguous and a separator-less key yields 2155 distinct values from 2155 lines.
It would pass every gate and both acceptance queries. That is the most dangerous shape a rule
can have -- it looks satisfied whatever you do. And a separator that can occur in a value does
not restore uniqueness anyway: measured, five distinct keys from six pairs.

So the decision is not which separator. It is that the composed key gets a generated check
against the source's own composite key, which turns three slices of asserted reasoning into
something falsifiable on the data that actually landed, whatever the separator and whatever the
parts turn out to be.

Two measurements changed what the rule says. `concat` is null-blind -- concat('1213','-',NULL)
is '1213-', not null -- so a missing half becomes a shorter key that collides with a real one;
`||` yields null and fails at the engine. And M2's stated reason for forbidding two entries was
simply wrong: they are refused at deploy, not silently loaded, and with allow_multiple_identifiers
set the entity key becomes a minted UUID with nothing in DAS to recompute it from, so the layer
stops being rebuildable. Both M2 and the dab skill are corrected where they stand.

Recorded and not fixed: the key expression cannot be changed after loading. Changing '-' to '/'
doubled everything -- 2155 keys to 4310, revenue 1,265,793 to 2,531,586 -- and `adss check`
caught it while naming a cause that has nothing to do with what happened.

c40557d docs(adr): let a stage be dated by a date it inherits, because a line has no date of its own
Slice 4 asks for revenue per order month, and the plan did not notice that an order line has
no date. The source's OrderDetail has five properties and not one is a date; the generator
can only date a stage by an attribute of the event's own entity; and no layer may go and fetch
one, because M1 forbids a join in a mapping's table and M5 forbids a reach into another table.
So the question as written could not be built at all. The failure was not even a refusal with
a reason -- a bare KeyError with nothing attached to it.

What makes the fix small is that the walk already exists. For every edge the generator already
resolves the parent as of the observation time of the row that inherits, and puts its key on
the child's bridge row; ADR 0006 spent its whole decision getting that instant right. A date is
another column of the row the walk has already found. It is also what a Unified Star Schema
means by a line's event: the event is the order being placed, on the day it was placed.

So date_attribute may name <ENTITY>.<ATTRIBUTE>, resolved in the same CTE and at the same
instant as the key, because they are the same row of the same parent. Two instants on one
bridge row is the confusion ADR 0006 calls the entire difference between the option it chose
and the one it rejected.

The cheap-looking option is the worst of them: expanding the source record so each line carries
its order's date would give PLACED_ON two homes, and two homes is how two reports start
disagreeing -- silently here, because both copies come from one load and would agree until the
first time they did not.

The record also closes the temptation it creates. The value is a date attribute of an entity
reached along a declared edge, resolved as its key is. Not an expression, and not a reach
further than the edges declared, however far the walk happens to go.

   282	def _inherit_cte(model: Model, event: Event, edge: Relationship) -> str:
   283	    """One inherited key: the pair in force when the inheriting row was observed. ADR 0006.
   284	
   285	    Resolved per inheriting ROW rather than per key -- the partition carries the observation
   286	    time -- because that is the whole reason ADR 0006 chose the observation time over "now".
   287	    A stage that kept more than the latest version of an entity would otherwise hand every one
   288	    of those versions the same parent, which is "as of now" wearing the other rule's clothes.
   289	
   290	    Read from `v_<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>`, which is the raw pairs plus the relationship's name, and
   291	    ranked here rather than by the engine. The engine's own ranked view answers a different
   292	    question -- who the parent is *now* -- and answers it with `rank()`, which returns two rows
   293	    for a child whose source named two parents at one instant. Two rows here would double that
   294	    child's measures, so the ranking is `row_number()` and the tie is refused by a data check.
   295	    """
   296	    source = model.entity(edge.source_entity_id)
   297	    target = model.entity(edge.target_entity_id)
   298	    held = edge.id.lower()
   299	    # If the event is dated by this target's attribute, the date is resolved here, off the same
   300	    # parent the key came from, so both are true as of one instant. ADR 0009.
   301	    inherited, attribute_id = event.dated_by
   302	    dates = inherited == target.id
   303	    carried = f",\n    cast(dated.{crossing(attribute_id)} AS DATE) AS _event_date" if dates else ""
   304	    joined = (
   305	        f'\nLEFT JOIN dab."view_{target.id}_hist" AS dated\n'
   306	        f"    ON dated.{crossing(target.source_key)} = pair.{crossing(target.source_key)}\n"
   307	        f"    AND dated.eff_tmstp <= revision._observed_at"
   308	        if dates
   309	        else ""
   310	    )

   312	        f"{event.name}__{held} AS (\n"
   313	        f"SELECT\n"
   314	        f"    revision.{source.key_column} AS {source.key_column},\n"
   315	        f"    revision._observed_at AS _observed_at,\n"
   316	        f"    pair.{crossing(target.source_key)} AS {target.key_column}"
   317	        f"{carried}\n"
   318	        f"FROM {event.name}__version AS revision\n"
   319	        f'LEFT JOIN dab."v_{edge.id}" AS pair\n'
   320	        f"    ON pair.{crossing(source.source_key)} = revision.{source.key_column}\n"
   321	        f"    AND pair.rel_name = '{edge.id}'\n"
   322	        f"    AND pair.row_st = 'Y'\n"
   323	        f"    AND pair.eff_tmstp <= revision._observed_at"
   324	        f"{joined}\n"
   325	        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
   326	        f"    PARTITION BY revision.{source.key_column}, revision._observed_at\n"
   327	        f"    ORDER BY\n"
   328	        f"        pair.eff_tmstp DESC,\n"
   329	        f"        pair.ver_tmstp DESC,\n"
   330	        f"        pair.{crossing(target.source_key)}"
   331	        + (",\n        dated.eff_tmstp ASC" if dates else "")
   332	        + "\n) = 1\n"
   333	        ")"
   334	    )

   337	def _stage_cte(model: Model, event: Event) -> str:
   338	    """One stage: the entity's version, with the key of everything it inherits from."""
   339	    entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
   340	    edges = model.edges_from(entity.id)
   341	    inherited, _ = event.dated_by
   342	    dater = "revision"
   343	    if inherited is not None:
   344	        dater = next(edge.id.lower() for edge in edges if edge.target_entity_id == inherited)
   345	    lines = [
   346	        f"    revision.{entity.key_column} AS {entity.key_column}",
   347	        "    revision._observed_at AS _observed_at",
   348	        f"    {dater}._event_date AS _event_date",
   349	    ]
   350	    lines += [
   351	        f"    {edge.id.lower()}.{model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column} "
   352	        f"AS {model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column}"
   353	        for edge in edges
   354	    ]
   355	    lines += [
   356	        f"    revision._measure__{entity.object_name}__{measure.id.lower()} "
   357	        f"AS _measure__{entity.object_name}__{measure.id.lower()}"
   358	        for measure in event.measures
   359	    ]
   360	    # One row per inheriting row in each of these, so none of the joins can fan out. LEFT
   361	    # anyway: the row that inherits nothing is kept by the join inside the CTE, and an inner
   362	    # join here would undo that one level up.
   363	    joins = "".join(
   364	        f"\nLEFT JOIN {event.name}__{edge.id.lower()} AS {edge.id.lower()}\n"
   365	        f"    ON {edge.id.lower()}.{entity.key_column} = revision.{entity.key_column}\n"
   366	        f"    AND {edge.id.lower()}._observed_at = revision._observed_at"
   367	        for edge in edges
   368	    )
   369	    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
   370	    # An event's own date is filtered in the version CTE; an inherited one is not there to
   371	    # filter, so it is filtered where it was resolved. Same rule, one step along the walk: a
   372	    # row whose date does not resolve is absent rather than dated null -- and the calendar's
   373	    # inner join would otherwise drop it silently, which looks like the rule working. ADR 0009.
   374	    absent = "" if inherited is None else f"\nWHERE {dater}._event_date IS NOT NULL"
   375	    return (
   376	        f"{event.name} AS (\nSELECT\n{selected}\n"
   377	        f"FROM {event.name}__version AS revision{joins}{absent}\n)"
   378	    )
   379	
   380	
   381	def _branch(model: Model, uss: Uss, event: Event, keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
   382	    """One branch of the union: this stage's own columns, and a typed NULL for the rest."""
   383	    entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
   384	    carried = {entity.key_column} | {
   385	        model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column for edge in model.edges_from(entity.id)
   386	    }
   387	    lines = [
   388	        f"    '{entity.object_name}' AS _stage",
   389	        f"    '{event.name}' AS _event",
   390	        f"    {event.name}._event_date AS _event_date",
   391	        "    TRUE AS _is_current",
   392	        f"    {event.name}._observed_at AS _observed_at",
   393	    ]
   394	    for key in keys:
   395	        value = f"{event.name}.{key}" if key in carried else "cast(NULL AS VARCHAR)"
   396	        lines.append(f"    {value} AS {key}")
   397	    owned = {column for candidate, _, column in uss.measure_columns() if candidate is event}
   398	    for _, measure, column in uss.measure_columns():
   399	        value = f"{event.name}.{column}" if column in owned else f"cast(NULL AS {measure.sql_type})"
   400	        lines.append(f"    {value} AS {column}")
   401	    return "SELECT\n" + ",\n".join(lines) + f"\nFROM {event.name} AS {event.name}"
   402	
   403	
   404	def entity_ids(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   405	    """Every entity the bridge names, in MODEL order: the ones with events, and the ones they
   406	    inherit from. An entity reached only by inheritance still needs a peripheral, or the bridge
   407	    carries a key that joins to nothing.
   408	    """
   409	    touched = {event.entity_id for event in uss.events}
   410	    touched |= {
   411	        edge.target_entity_id for event in uss.events for edge in model.edges_from(event.entity_id)
   412	    }
   413	    return tuple(entity.id for entity in model.entities if entity.id in touched)
   414	
   415	
   416	def entity_keys(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   417	    """One key column per entity the bridge names, in MODEL order.
   418	
   419	    Model order, not event order: reordering two events in the sidecar is not a model change,
   420	    and it must not rearrange a contract that consumers are written against. The check cannot
   421	    catch that on its own, because it derives what it expects from this same function.
   422	    """
   423	    return tuple(model.entity(entity_id).key_column for entity_id in entity_ids(model, uss))
   424	
   425	
   426	def bridge_columns(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   427	    """The published column contract, in order.
   428	
   429	    Grouped: the structural columns, then one key per entity in model order, then one column
   430	    per measure in declaration order.
   431	
   432	    That grouping means the contract does NOT only ever grow at the end, and saying otherwise
   433	    would be the more comfortable lie. A new entity appends a key, and because keys precede
   434	    measures, every measure column moves right. An entity inserted in the middle of the model
   435	    moves the keys after it as well. So the model file's own order is part of this contract,
   436	    and nothing here can catch a rearrangement: the check that compares the built bridge to
   437	    this contract derives what it expects from this same function, so both sides move together
   438	    and it passes either way.
   439	
   440	    What makes that tolerable rather than a defect is that nothing reads this table by
   441	    position. Conventions section 3 forbids `SELECT *`, the questions name their columns and
   442	    so does the destination. A consumer that did read positionally would be reading a contract
   443	    this docstring does not offer it. New entities still go at the end, because moving a key
   444	    column is a bigger change than moving a measure. Blueprint B7.
   445	    """
   446	    keys = entity_keys(model, uss)
   447	    structural = ("_stage", "_event", "_event_date", "_is_current", "_observed_at")
   448	    return structural + keys + tuple(column for _, _, column in uss.measure_columns())
   449	
   450	
   451	def bridge_sql(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> str:
   452	    """One row per measurement event, over every stage the declarations name."""
   453	    keys = entity_keys(model, uss)
   454	    ctes = ",\n\n".join(
   455	        cte
   456	        for event in uss.events
   457	        for cte in (
   458	            _version_cte(model, event),
   459	            *(_inherit_cte(model, event, edge) for edge in model.edges_from(event.entity_id)),
   460	            _stage_cte(model, event),
   461	        )
   462	    )
   463	    branches = "\n\nUNION ALL\n\n".join(_branch(model, uss, event, keys) for event in uss.events)
   464	    return f"{_GENERATED}\nCREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {BRIDGE.sql} AS\nWITH {ctes}\n\n{branches};\n"
   465	
   466	
   467	def peripheral_sql(model: Model, entity_id: str) -> str:
   468	    """One row per entity instance, current state, key first and attributes as declared."""
   469	    entity: Entity = model.entity(entity_id)
   470	    lines = [
   471	        f"    e.{crossing(entity.source_key)} AS {entity.key_column}",
   472	        "    e.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at",
   473	    ]
   474	    lines += [f"    e.{crossing(a.id)} AS {a.column}" for a in entity.attributes]
   475	    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
   476	    relation = Relation(Schema.DAR_USS, entity.object_name)
   477	    return (
   478	        f"{_GENERATED}\n"
   479	        f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {relation.sql} AS\n"
   480	        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
   481	        f'FROM dab."view_{entity.id}_hist" AS e\n'
   482	        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
   483	        f"    PARTITION BY e.{crossing(entity.source_key)}\n"
   484	        f"    ORDER BY e.eff_tmstp DESC\n"
   485	        f") = 1;\n"
   486	    )
   487	
   488	
   489	def calendar_sql() -> str:
   490	    """Dense and daily across everything the bridge holds. Civil arithmetic only.
   491	
   492	    A calendar containing only the days something happened is not a calendar: a month with
   493	    no events must still appear in a time series. Fiscal periods and holidays are business
   494	    meaning and would need a definition, so they belong in the model, not in a generator.
   495	    """
   496	    return (
   497	        f"{_GENERATED}\n"
   498	        f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {CALENDAR.sql} AS\n"
   499	        f"WITH bounds AS (\n"
   500	        f"SELECT\n"
   501	        f"    min(b._event_date) AS first_date,\n"
   502	        f"    max(b._event_date) AS last_date\n"
   503	        f"FROM {BRIDGE.sql} AS b\n"
   504	        f"),\n\n"
   505	        f"every_day AS (\n"
   506	        f"SELECT\n"
   507	        f"    cast(d.day AS DATE) AS date_key\n"
   508	        f"FROM bounds AS bo\n"
   509	        f"CROSS JOIN range(\n"
   510	        f"    bo.first_date, bo.last_date + INTERVAL 1 DAY, INTERVAL 1 DAY\n"
   511	        f") AS d (day)\n"
   512	        f")\n\n"
   513	        f"SELECT\n"
   514	        f"    d.date_key AS date_key,\n"
   515	        f"    cast(year(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS year_number,\n"
   516	        f"    cast(quarter(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS quarter_of_year,\n"
   517	        f"    cast(month(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS month_of_year,\n"
   518	        f"    cast(day(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS day_of_month,\n"
   519	        f"    cast(date_trunc('year', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS year_start,\n"
   520	        f"    cast(date_trunc('quarter', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS quarter_start,\n"
   521	        f"    cast(date_trunc('month', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS month_start,\n"
   522	        f"    strftime(d.date_key, '%Y') || '-Q' || cast(quarter(d.date_key) AS VARCHAR) "
   523	        f"AS quarter_label,\n"
   524	        f"    strftime(d.date_key, '%Y-%m') AS month_label\n"
   525	        f"FROM every_day AS d;\n"
   526	    )
   527	
   528	
   529	def definitions(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> dict[str, str]:
   530	    """Every definition, by the token that refers to it. Copied verbatim, never composed.
   531	
   532	    A generator that composed a definition would be a third place the data is explained,
   533	    and the worst kind: one nobody wrote and nobody reviews.
   534	    """
   535	    found = dict(model.definitions())
   536	    for event in uss.events:
   537	        found[f"{event.entity_id}.events.{event.id}"] = event.definition
   538	        for measure in event.measures:
   539	            found[f"{event.entity_id}.measures.{measure.id}"] = measure.definition
   540	    return found

   288	    ] = False,

   302	    kept = {

   315	            typer.echo(f"removed {orphan.relative_to(project.root)}")

    61	def run_checks(project: Project, connection: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> list[Finding]:
    62	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    63	
    64	    model = read_model(project.model)
    65	    uss = read_uss(project.uss, model)
    66	    described = [name for name, *_ in connection.execute("DESCRIBE dar__uss._bridge").fetchall()]
    67	    expected = list(bridge_columns(model, uss))
    68	    findings.append(
    69	        Finding(
    70	            "the bridge matches its published column contract",
    71	            described == expected,
    72	            f"built {described}, contract {expected}",
    73	        )
    74	    )
    75	
    76	    # Every generated data check, over every contract. Growing the layer grows the checks.
    77	    for path in sorted(project.checks_sql.glob("*.sql")):
    78	        passed, detail = _zero(connection, path.read_text())
    79	        findings.append(
    80	            Finding(f"{path.stem}: nothing disagrees", passed, f"{detail} disagreements")
    81	        )
    82	
    83	    # The engine behaviours the generated layer is built on. If the vendor changes any of
    84	    # them, this says so rather than the star schema quietly emptying.
    85	    for entity in model.entities:
    86	        for suffix in ("focal", "idfr"):
    87	            rows = connection.execute(f'SELECT count(*) FROM dab."{entity.id}_{suffix}"').fetchone()
    88	            findings.append(
    89	                Finding(
    90	                    f"dab.{entity.id}_{suffix} is still empty, as the generator assumes",
    91	                    rows == (0,),
    92	                    f"{rows} rows -- if this is no longer 0 the generator should read it",
    93	                )
    94	            )
    95	        # `view_<E>_with_rel` is not one behaviour but two, and the name says neither. On an
    96	        # edge's SOURCE side it is a passthrough. On its TARGET side it becomes a join back to
    97	        # the source entity, carrying that entity's key AND all its attributes, one row per
    98	        # source row -- so summing a target's own measure over it multiplies. Slice 1 asserted
    99	        # the passthrough of every entity, which was only ever true because it had no edges.
   100	        with_rel = _columns(connection, f"view_{entity.id}_with_rel")
   101	        plain = _columns(connection, f"view_{entity.id}")
   102	        inbound = [e for e in model.relationships if e.target_entity_id == entity.id]
   103	        fanned = plain + [
   104	            c for e in inbound for c in _columns(connection, f"view_{e.source_entity_id}")
   105	        ]
   106	        findings.append(
   107	            Finding(
   108	                f"dab.view_{entity.id}_with_rel is what a {'target' if inbound else 'source'} "
   109	                f"side looks like",
   110	                with_rel == fanned,
   111	                f"with_rel {with_rel} vs expected {fanned} -- if this changed, the generator's "
   112	                f"reason for never reading this view has changed with it",
   113	            )
   114	        )
   115	
   116	    # The one engine behaviour the whole as-of rule rests on, and the only one not pinned
   117	    # until now: that `v_<edge>` hands over the RAW pairs. If a release added ranking inside
   118	    # it, the rule ADR 0006 spends generated SQL to own would silently revert to the vendor's
   119	    # "as of now", and every check and both questions would still pass. Pinned two ways: it
   120	    # still exposes the columns only an unranked read has, and it still returns every row the
   121	    # pair table holds for that relationship.
   122	    for edge in model.relationships:
   123	        exposed = _columns(connection, f"v_{edge.id}")
   124	        findings.append(
   125	            Finding(
   126	                f"dab.v_{edge.id} still hands over the raw pairs",
   127	                {"row_st", "ver_tmstp", "rel_name"} <= set(exposed),
   128	                f"{exposed} -- the ranked view drops row_st and ver_tmstp, so losing them "
   129	                f"here means this object has become a ranked one and the as-of rule is the "
   130	                f"vendor's again",
   131	            )
   132	        )
   133	        counted = connection.execute(
   134	            f'SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM dab."v_{edge.id}" WHERE rel_name = ?), '
   135	            f'(SELECT count(*) FROM dab."{edge.source_entity_id}_{edge.target_entity_id}_x")',
   136	            [edge.id],
   137	        ).fetchone()
   138	        through, raw = counted if counted else (None, None)
   139	        findings.append(
   140	            Finding(
   141	                f"dab.v_{edge.id} filters nothing out of the pair table",
   142	                through == raw,
   143	                f"{through} through the view, {raw} in the pair table -- a gap means the view "
   144	                f"has started ranking or filtering, and the generator ranks it a second time",
   145	            )
   146	        )

   149	    # only place: every presentation view hides it.
   150	    for entity in model.entities:
   151	        described_rows = connection.execute(
   152	            f'SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT ("{entity.id}_key", type_key, eff_tmstp)) '
   153	            f'FROM dab."{entity.id}_desc"'
   154	        ).fetchone()
   155	        total, distinct = described_rows if described_rows else (None, None)
   156	        findings.append(
   157	            Finding(
   158	                f"dab.{entity.id}_desc holds no duplicate versions",
   159	                total == distinct,
   160	                f"{total} rows, {distinct} distinct -- a growing gap is FULL ingestion "
   161	                f"duplicating silently",

   163	        )
   164	
   165	    for question in read_questions(project.questions):
   166	        if question.status in (Status.DRAFT, Status.SUPERSEDED):
   167	            findings.append(

   170	                    True,
   171	                    "a draft is not finished and a superseded question is not asked any more; "
   172	                    "running either would fail the build on something nobody is answering",
   173	                )
   174	            )

   177	        answer = _rows(connection, question.uss_sql)
   178	        # The comparison below is row by row, by value, which is exact only while every value
   179	        # is. A float would make it order-dependent rather than wrong: DuckDB's sum over

   184	        loose = inexact((*control, *answer))

   190	                f"and an inexact value makes this comparison order-dependent",
   191	            )
   192	        )
   193	        findings.append(
   194	            Finding(
   195	                f"{question.id}: the source and the star schema agree",
   196	                control == answer,
   197	                f"{len(control)} control rows, {len(answer)} answer rows"
   198	                + (
   199	                    "" if control == answer else f"; first difference {_first_gap(control, answer)}"
   200	                ),
   201	            )
   202	        )
   203	    return findings

   206	def contracts_of(project: Project) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   207	    """Every contract this project declares, by the object it generates.
   208	
   209	    Two commands write into `checks/` and each sweeps what neither generates, so each has to
   210	    know the other's file names. This is how the DAR generator knows which files belong to a
   211	    contract without reading contracts for anything else.
   212	    """
   213	    return tuple(read_contract(path).table for path in project.contract_paths())

   216	def relationship_check_names(model: Model) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   217	    """What relationship_checks would be called, without emitting or formatting any of it.
   218	
   219	    The contract side of `checks/` only needs the names, to leave these files alone. Building
   220	    the SQL for that would run the fixer over every check and throw the result away, which
   221	    also makes a DAS command fail when the DAB model is unreadable.
   222	    """
   223	    return tuple(
   224	        f"{edge.id.lower()}__{suffix}.sql"
   225	        for edge in model.relationships
   226	        for suffix in ("one_target", "loaded", "resolves")
   227	    )
   228	
   229	
   230	_EDGE = "-- Generated from dab/model.yaml. Do not edit; regenerate with `adss dar generate`."
   231	
   232	
   233	def relationship_checks(model: Model) -> dict[str, str]:
   234	    """One check per way an edge fails without saying so. ADR 0006.
   235	
   236	    All three failures look identical in the built warehouse -- an inherited key that is null,
   237	    or wrong, on rows that look like data rather than like a defect -- and none of them is
   238	    reported by the engine at deploy, at execute, or by a question's acceptance queries.
   239	    """
   240	    generated: dict[str, str] = {}
   241	    for edge in model.relationships:
   242	        source = model.entity(edge.source_entity_id)
   243	        target = model.entity(edge.target_entity_id)
   244	        pairs = f'dab."v_{edge.id}"'
   245	        open_pairs = (
   246	            f"FROM {pairs} AS pair\nWHERE pair.rel_name = '{edge.id}'\n    AND pair.row_st = 'Y'"
   247	        )
   248	        name = edge.id.lower()
   249	
   250	        # The generator resolves a tie with row_number(), so it can never fan out -- but
   251	        # resolving a tie deterministically is still choosing arbitrarily between two answers.
   252	        generated[f"{name}__one_target"] = (
   253	            f"{_EDGE}\n"
   254	            f"SELECT count(*) AS ambiguities\n"
   255	            f"FROM (\n"
   256	            f"    SELECT\n"
   257	            f"        pair.{crossing(source.source_key)} AS source_key,\n"
   258	            f"        pair.eff_tmstp AS observed_at\n"
   259	            f"    {open_pairs}\n"
   260	            f"    GROUP BY pair.{crossing(source.source_key)}, pair.eff_tmstp\n"
   261	            f"    HAVING count(DISTINCT pair.{crossing(target.source_key)}) > 1\n"
   262	            f") AS tied;\n"
   263	        )
   264	
   265	        # An edge that loaded nothing is what a mis-spelled M6 source_table looks like: the
   266	        # engine skips the relationship in silence and every inherited key is null.
   267	        generated[f"{name}__loaded"] = (
   268	            f"{_EDGE}\n"
   269	            f"SELECT count(*) AS unloaded\n"
   270	            f"FROM (SELECT 1 AS declared) AS edge\n"
   271	            f"WHERE NOT EXISTS (\n"
   272	            f"    SELECT 1\n"
   273	            f"    {open_pairs}\n"
   274	            f");\n"
   275	        )
   276	
   277	        # And a target expression of the wrong shape loads pairs that join to nothing.
   278	        generated[f"{name}__resolves"] = (
   279	            f"{_EDGE}\n"
   280	            f"SELECT count(*) AS dangling\n"
   281	            f"FROM {BRIDGE.sql} AS b\n"
   282	            f"LEFT JOIN {Relation(Schema.DAR_USS, target.object_name).sql} AS t\n"
   283	            f"    ON b.{target.key_column} = t.{target.key_column}\n"
   284	            f"WHERE b._stage = '{source.object_name}'\n"
   285	            f"    AND b.{target.key_column} IS NOT NULL\n"
   286	            f"    AND t.{target.key_column} IS NULL;\n"
   287	        )
   288	    return generated

            f"    FROM {current.sql}\n"
            f") AS counted\n"

def measure_check_names(uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """What measure_checks would be called, without emitting or formatting any of it.

    The contract side of `checks/` only needs the names, to leave these files alone -- the same
    reason relationship_check_names exists, and the same cost: a DAS command now reads the
    declarations to learn what it must not delete.
    """
    return tuple(
        f"{column.removeprefix('_')}__isolated.sql" for _, _, column in uss.measure_columns()
    )


def measure_checks(uss: Uss) -> dict[str, str]:
    """One check per measure: it is non-null on its own event's rows and on no other. ADR 0012.

    This is the property D-0001 rests on, carried into every build. `tests/test_fan_out.py`
    proves it with numbers on a warehouse it builds; this asserts the mechanism on the warehouse
    that was actually built, where a wrong number would be believed.

    By EVENT and not by stage. Two events on one entity share a stage, so a per-stage check would
    let a parent's shipment measure sit on its placement row and report nothing -- and that is the
    likelier defect, since every branch of the union comes off the same stage's CTE.

    It counts leaks only. A measure that is null everywhere would pass here, and is not this
    check's to catch: a bridge that lost its rows disagrees with the source, which is what
    `adss questions check` compares on every build.
    """
    return {
        f"{column.removeprefix('_')}__isolated": (
            f"{_MEASURE}\n"
            f"SELECT count(*) AS leaked\n"
            f"FROM {BRIDGE.sql} AS b\n"
            f"WHERE b._event != '{event.name}'\n"
            f"    AND b.{column} IS NOT NULL;\n"
        )
        for event, _, column in uss.measure_columns()
    }


def _first_gap(control: list[tuple[object, ...]], answer: list[tuple[object, ...]]) -> str:
    for index, (left, right) in enumerate(zip(control, answer, strict=False)):
        if left != right:
            return f"row {index}: source {left} vs star {right}"
    return f"lengths differ: {len(control)} vs {len(answer)}"

"""DAS in SQL: a forgiving view over what landed, and a strict view over what was declared.

Nothing here interprets. A cast records what the source's own metadata says a field is; the
format has no way to express anything more, which is what keeps the layer honest. ADR 0003.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from adss.contract import ColumnType, Contract
from adss.names import Relation, Schema

# The provenance this layer adds itself, named for what it records rather than for whoever
# wrote it. Blueprint S4.
PROVENANCE = ("source_system", "source_entity", "source_url")

# Every name this layer adds for itself. A contract may not land a source field under one:
# the warehouse would silently rename the duplicate rather than refuse it.
RESERVED = frozenset({*PROVENANCE, "payload", "extracted_at", "extracted_on"})

_GENERATED = "-- Generated from das/contracts/{table}.yaml. Do not edit; edit the contract."


def _extract(column_type: ColumnType, source_path: str, sql_type: str) -> str:
    """The one expression per type. This dictionary is where staging decisions accumulate."""
    path = f"'$.{source_path}'"
    if column_type is ColumnType.STRING:
        return f"landed.payload ->> {path}"
    if column_type is ColumnType.JSON:
        return f"landed.payload -> {path}"
    return f"cast(landed.payload ->> {path} AS {sql_type})"


def raw_view_sql(contract: Contract, lake: Path) -> str:
    """One view per contract over the append-only hive-partitioned lake.

    Both read options are correctness rather than taste: without union_by_name a column that
    appears only in later loads is silently dropped, and without hive_types the partition key
    comes back as text.
    """
    relation = Relation(Schema.DAS_RAW, contract.table)
    glob = lake / contract.table / "extracted_on=*" / "*.parquet"
    landed = ["payload", *PROVENANCE, "extracted_on", "_dlt_load_id", "_dlt_id"]
    selected = ",\n".join(f"    landed.{name} AS {name}" for name in landed)
    return (
        f"{_GENERATED.format(table=contract.table)}\n"
        f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {relation.sql} AS\n"
        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
        f"FROM read_parquet(\n"
        f"    '{glob}',\n"
        f"    hive_partitioning => true,\n"
        f"    hive_types => {{ 'extracted_on': 'DATE' }},\n"
        f"    union_by_name => true\n"
        f") AS landed;\n"
    )


def staged_view_sql(contract: Contract) -> str:
    """The change log: one row per source record per load, strictly typed.

    The payload is deliberately absent. If it were here a downstream mapping could read
    straight out of it and the contract would stop being the gate.
    """
    relation = Relation(Schema.DAS_STAGED, contract.table)
    lines = [
        f"    {_extract(column.type, column.source_path, column.sql_type)} AS {column.target_name}"
        for column in contract.columns
    ]
    lines += [f"    landed.{name} AS {name}" for name in PROVENANCE]
    lines.append("    to_timestamp(cast(landed._dlt_load_id AS DOUBLE)) AS extracted_at")
    lines.append("    landed.extracted_on AS extracted_on")
    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
    return (
        f"{_GENERATED.format(table=contract.table)}\n"
        f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {relation.sql} AS\n"
        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
        f"FROM {Relation(Schema.DAS_RAW, contract.table).sql} AS landed;\n"
    )


def current_view_sql(contract: Contract) -> str:
    """One row per key, from the latest load that carried it.

    A question asked of the source needs one row per thing, not one per observation. The
    change log beside it is what DAB historizes from.
    """
    relation = Relation(Schema.DAS_STAGED, f"{contract.table}__current")
    names = [column.target_name for column in contract.columns]
    names += [*PROVENANCE, "extracted_at", "extracted_on"]
    selected = ",\n".join(f"    staged.{name} AS {name}" for name in names)
    partition = ", ".join(f"staged.{key}" for key in contract.primary_keys)
    return (
        f"{_GENERATED.format(table=contract.table)}\n"
        f"CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {relation.sql} AS\n"
        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
        f"FROM {Relation(Schema.DAS_STAGED, contract.table).sql} AS staged\n"
        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
        f"    PARTITION BY {partition}\n"
        f"    ORDER BY staged.extracted_at DESC\n"
        f") = 1;\n"
    )


def lake_dir(root: Path) -> Path:
    """Where the landing zone actually sits under the lake root.

    The loader writes its dataset name into the path, and the dataset name is the schema.
    """
    return root / str(Schema.DAS_RAW)


def clock_check_sql(contract: Contract) -> str:
    """The partition key and the observation clock derive from one fact and must agree.

    The comparison is pinned to UTC. `extracted_at` is a TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, so casting
    it to a date resolves in the reader's session timezone, while the partition key is the
    loader's UTC date -- and the check would then fail on every machine east or west of
    Greenwich for a warehouse that is perfectly correct.

    Emitted per contract rather than written in Python: the machinery must work for any
    source, so it may not name one, and SQL in a string is SQL the linter never sees.
    """
    relation = Relation(Schema.DAS_STAGED, contract.table)
    return (
        f"{_GENERATED.format(table=contract.table)}\n"
        f"SELECT count(*) AS disagreements\n"
        f"FROM {relation.sql} AS staged\n"
        f"WHERE staged.extracted_on <> cast(timezone('UTC', staged.extracted_at) AS DATE);\n"
    )


def key_check_sql(contract: Contract) -> str:
    """One row per key in the current view, however many loads the change log holds."""
    current = Relation(Schema.DAS_STAGED, f"{contract.table}__current")

    # composite key needs its parts made into one value -- and grouping parentheses do not

    # one that cannot run. It is a function call now, which the formatter has no licence to
    # unwrap. An unrunnable check aborts the whole run before a finding is printed.

     2	
     3	Nothing here decides what a field is. The record arrives as one JSON value and stays that
     4	way, so a field the contract has never heard of still lands and is simply not yet
     5	extracted -- which is what makes an upstream change a contract edit rather than an outage.
     6	ADR 0003.
     7	"""

     9	from __future__ import annotations
    10	
    11	from collections.abc import Iterator
    12	from pathlib import Path
    13	from typing import Any
    14	
    15	import dlt
    16	from dlt.destinations import filesystem
    17	
    18	from adss.contract import Contract
    19	from adss.names import Schema
    20	from adss.source import Fetch, pages
    21	
    22	# The load's own clock names the partition. Placeholders are the loader's, and it rejects
    23	# any it does not know, so a typo here fails loudly rather than landing somewhere odd.
    24	LAYOUT = "{table_name}/extracted_on={YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{load_id}.{file_id}.{ext}"
    25	
    26	
    27	def land(contract: Contract, fetch: Fetch, root: Path, pipelines_dir: Path) -> list[str]:
    28	    """Append one load of one contract's entity set to the lake. Returns the load ids."""
    29	
    30	    @dlt.resource(  # type: ignore[misc]
    31	        name=contract.table,
    32	        write_disposition="append",
    33	        columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}},
    34	    )
    35	    def records() -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    36	        for url, page in pages(contract.source, fetch):
    37	            for record in page:
    38	                # payload is a single json-typed column, so nothing inside it is inferred,
    39	                # split into columns, or promoted to a child table.
    40	                yield {
    41	                    "payload": record,
    42	                    "source_system": contract.source.service,
    43	                    "source_entity": contract.source.entity,
    44	                    "source_url": url,
    45	                }
    46	
    47	    destination = filesystem(
    48	        bucket_url=root.absolute().as_uri(),
    49	        layout=LAYOUT,
    50	        # Without this the dataset name is normalised and das__raw quietly becomes das_raw,
    51	        # with only a warning to say so.
    52	        enable_dataset_name_normalization=False,
    53	    )
    54	    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    55	        pipeline_name=f"adss_das_{contract.table}",
    56	        destination=destination,
    57	        dataset_name=str(Schema.DAS_RAW),
    58	        pipelines_dir=str(pipelines_dir),
    59	    )
    60	    info = pipeline.run(records(), loader_file_format="parquet")
    61	    return list(info.loads_ids)

     7	
     8	# A stage may be dated by a date it inherits along the walk, named where it is inherited from
     9	
    10	## Context and Problem Statement
    11	
    12	Slice 4 asks for revenue per order **month**. Revenue is measured on an order line — quantity
    13	times price less discount — so the bridge needs a row per line. And **an order line has no
    14	date.** The source's `OrderDetail` has five properties and not one of them is a date; the live
    15	`$metadata` says so, and there is nothing to map from.
    16	
    17	The generator can only date a stage by an attribute of the event's own entity. `read_uss`
    18	resolves `date_attribute` against `model.entity(event.entity_id)`, so naming the order's date on
    19	a line event fails with a bare `KeyError: "ORDER_LINE has no attribute 'PLACED_ON'"` — not even a
    20	`UssError`, so the refusal arrives with no explanation attached.
    21	
    22	Nor may any layer go and fetch one. M1 forbids a join or a subquery in a mapping's `table:`; M5
    23	forbids a reach into another table; a DAS contract has no key for a join. A second mapped table
    24	on `ORDER_LINE` would be keyed by the order, which is not a line.
    25	
    26	So the question the plan wrote down for this slice cannot be built at all without deciding
    27	something the plan did not anticipate.
    28	
    29	**What is already true, and is the whole reason this is small.** The walk exists. For every
    30	edge, `_inherit_cte` already resolves the parent **as of the observation time of the row that
    31	inherits** and puts the parent's key on the child's bridge row. ADR 0006 spent its whole decision
    32	on getting that instant right. A date is another column of the row the walk already found.
    33	
    34	This is also what a Unified Star Schema does. Puppini's bridge is a row per measurement event;
    35	the event for an order line is the order being placed, on the day it was placed. Dating a line by
    36	its order's date is not an accommodation — it is what the shape means.
    37	
    38	## Decision Drivers
    39	
    40	* the question is answerable at all, which today it is not
    41	* a bridge row is true as of one instant, and every column on it is true as of that same instant
    42	* a mechanism that already exists, extended, rather than a second one beside it
    43	* the date a reader sees is traceable to a definition in the one place data is explained
    44	* slice 5 walks two hops, and must not need a third mechanism
    45	
    46	## Considered Options
    47	
    48	* **(a)** The date inherits along the walk, named as `<ENTITY>.<ATTRIBUTE>` in the sidecar
    49	* **(b)** Record `OrderDetails?$expand=Order` so the landed line carries the order's date
    50	* **(c)** Give `ORDER_LINE` its own date attribute, mapped from the order via the source
    51	* **(d)** Drop the calendar and let the question group on the order peripheral's date
    52	
    53	## Decision Outcome
    54	
    55	Chosen: **(a), the date inherits along the walk**, written in `dab/uss.yaml` as
    56	
    57	```yaml
    58	    - id: ORDERED
    59	      entity: ORDER_LINE
    60	      date_attribute: ORDER.PLACED_ON      # qualified: inherited along the edge to ORDER
    61	```
    62	
    63	An unqualified `date_attribute` still means an attribute of the event's own entity, which is
    64	every event declared so far and stays the ordinary case. A qualified one names the entity the
    65	date is inherited from, and that entity must be reachable along a declared edge from the event's
    66	entity — otherwise it is refused, by name, with the edges that do exist listed.
    67	
    68	The date is resolved **in the same CTE and at the same instant as the key**, because they are the
    69	same row of the same parent. Anything else would put two instants on one bridge row, which is the
    70	confusion ADR 0006 calls the entire difference between the option it chose and the one it
    71	rejected. A line whose order cannot be resolved gets a null date and therefore no bridge row, by
    72	the filter the generator already emits — consistent with how an event that did not happen is
    73	already handled.
    74	
    75	**Why not (b), expanding the source record.** It is the cheap-looking one and it is the worst.
    76	`PLACED_ON` would then have two homes — the order's own attribute and a copy on every line — and
    77	B8 says a definition exists exactly once. Two homes is how two reports start disagreeing, and
    78	this one would disagree *silently*, because both copies come from the same load and would agree
    79	until the first time they did not. It also needs a new contract key and a new `Endpoint` field to
    80	build a URL the recorder cannot currently express.
    81	
    82	**Why not (c), a mapped date on the line.** Same objection with an extra step: the mapping would
    83	have to reach into another table to get it, which M5 forbids outright.
    84	
    85	**Why not (d), grouping on the peripheral.** The stage still needs a non-null date to exist at
    86	all, so it does not escape the problem. And ADR 0007 rejected the peripheral-as-of-now reasoning
    87	already: a peripheral is current state, a bridge row is the version in which the event is dated,
    88	and reading one against the other puts two instants on one answer.
    89	
    90	### What this does not become
    91	
    92	The temptation this record exists to close is to let `date_attribute` take an expression, or to
    93	let it reach further than one declared edge because "the walk goes there anyway". Neither. The
    94	value is *a date attribute of an entity reached along a declared edge*, resolved exactly as its
    95	key is resolved. Arithmetic on it belongs in the mapping under ADR 0007; anything else is a
    96	second expression language in a file that is not linted, which ADR 0007 refused on §3.
    97	
    98	## Consequences
    99	
   100	* Good, because the question is answerable, and answerable at the grain it is asked at
   101	* Good, because it reuses the walk rather than adding a mechanism beside it: one more column off
   102	  a row the generator already resolves, at an instant it already got right
   103	* Good, because slice 5's two-hop chain inherits this unchanged — a date reached along two edges
   104	  is the same rule applied twice, and needs no new decision
   105	* Good, because the date on a line is traceable to `ORDER.PLACED_ON`, which has one definition,
   106	  so the page's glossary can explain the axis a reader is looking at
   107	* Bad, because `dab/uss.yaml` now has two shapes for one field, and a reader has to know that a
   108	  dot means "inherited". The alternative — always qualifying — would rewrite three existing
   109	  declarations for no gain, and `<ENTITY>.<ATTRIBUTE>` is the notation the questions already use
   110	* Bad, because a line's date now moves if its order is re-pointed to a different order, which
   111	  cannot happen in this source and is a real property of the design rather than a bug. The
   112	  as-of resolution is what bounds it: the date is the one in force when the line was observed
   113	
   114	## Confirmation
   115	
   116	`tests/test_uss.py` asserts that a qualified `date_attribute` is resolved from the inherited
   117	entity and not from the event's own; that it is refused, naming the available edges, when the
   118	entity it names is not reachable along one; that an unqualified one still means the event's own
   119	entity; and that the date and the key come from the same CTE, so no bridge row can carry two
   120	instants. The neutral fixture gains an event on `CHILD` dated by `PARENT.HAPPENED_ON`, which is
   121	the shape this record is about and which the fixture did not have.
   122	
   123	A data check asserts that every bridge row's `_event_date` for such a stage equals the inherited
   124	entity's own date for the key on that row — the property that would break silently if the two
   125	were ever resolved at different instants.

def read_question(directory: Path) -> Question:
    text = (directory / "question.md").read_text()
    parsed = FRONT_MATTER.match(text)
    if parsed is None:
        raise QuestionError(f"{directory}: question.md has no front matter")
    front = yaml.safe_load(parsed.group(1))

    # separator, or be anything a shell or a path would read as more than a name. An empty one
    # is the worst of them: it means "every question" to the page, so the record of what was
    # delivered for this question would quietly be a picture of all of them.
    identifier = str(front["id"])
    if not ID.match(identifier):
        raise QuestionError(
            f"{directory}: {identifier!r} is not a usable question id. It names a file and an "
            f"environment variable, so it must be lower-case letters, digits, hyphen and "
            f"underscore, and must not be empty."
        )
    return Question(
        directory=directory,
        id=identifier,
        status=Status(str(front["status"])),
        persona=str(front["persona"]),
        question=str(front["question"]),
        dimensions=tuple(str(d) for d in front["dimensions"]),

        staged_sql=(directory / STAGED).read_text(),

        raise QuestionError(f"{question.id}: declares {missing}, which nothing defines")
